thread:
maya: Quick sync — product wants a clear, consistent client surface for quota vs capacity vs graceful fallback. Proposal: keep standard HTTP for obvious cases (429 quota, 403 auth, 503 capacity), but when we intentionally serve a lower-quality fallback model return 200 + body { "routed_to": "small-model", "status": "DEGRADED", "reason": "capacity_burst" }. This lets frontends show a badge. Opinions?
kevin: +1 to using 429/503. question: do we need a distinct 424 or 409 for 'degraded by policy' vs 'fallback due to node failure'?
sanjay: telemetry-wise it's easiest if we also emit an `X-Redwood-Status` header with compact token values so downstream logs can aggregate without parsing bodies. e.g. `X-Redwood-Status: OK`, `DEGRADED`, `FALLBACK`, `QUOTA`. We can also include `X-Redwood-Route` for model variant.
lina: Console UX: prefer a single canonical signal to drive the badge + runbook link. header + body status is fine. Make the runbook link resolvable from header like `X-Redwood-Runbook: /rb/456`.
product_jamie: from product POV, wording matters. Client-facing copy should avoid jargon — prefer "We served a lower-fidelity response to keep latency low" vs "DEGRADED" in UI. We still need internal tokens for telemetry.
ellen: SDKs should surface both: `response.meta.status` (enum) + `status_code` and `headers`. Backwards compatibility: if older SDKs expect 200 for content, we mustn't break them. So fallback should usually be 200 with `meta.status != OK`.
kevin: if we return 200 for fallback, how do clients detect severe failures? e.g., we want non-200 for terminal failures so clients can retry. Maybe policy: terminal errors -> 4xx/5xx, graceful fallbacks -> 200 w/ status=DEGRADED.
sanjay: agree. add metrics: increment `redwood.client_signal{status="DEGRADED",route="small-model"}` and ensure trace/span tag `redwood.signal=DEGRADED` so we can pivot metrics/dashboards.
lina: dashboard ask: add badges for percent of responses with status != OK per route, with trendline and 95th latency for degraded responses. Also a quick filter to show runbook hits.
maya: rollout plan: implement header + meta in API, ship server-side flag `status-signal-v1` and enable canary on 5% of hosts. We'll backfill old telemetry by mapping fallback logs -> DEGRAD. deploy-bot will create canary.
deploy-bot: Canary created: feature=status-signal-v1, env=canary, hosts=5%, started 2024-10-08T15:12Z :rocket:
kevin: small nit — for quota we should include `Retry-After` and `X-Quota-Remaining`. product_jamie: yes, and console should surface a CTA: "request more capacity" when X-Quota-Remaining=0.
ellen: quick code sample for SDK docs:
```
if (resp.meta.status !== 'OK') {
  showBanner('Quality reduced to preserve latency')
}
if (resp.headers['x-redwood-status'] === 'QUOTA') {
  // show quota CTA
}
```
maya: excellent. action items: 1) eng-runtime to add headers + body field (owner: sanjay) 2) console to add badge/filter (owner: lina) 3) product to sign off UI copy (owner: product_jamie) 4) SDKs to add helpers (owner: ellen). I'll open RFC and schedule a 30m sync tomorrow. :calendar:
lina: sgtm :thumbsup:
kevin: sgtm
sanjay: will start a PR today
product_jamie: will draft UX copy and link in RFC
ellen: will add SDK helper prototype
maya: thanks everyone — let's keep messages short in RFC thread so it's easy to follow. :party:
